headline_marked: Tawhid Hridoy hits [[unbeaten 242]] to set new Bangladesh Test record
headline: Tawhid Hridoy hits unbeaten 242 to set new Bangladesh Test record
summary: Tawhid Hridoy smashed an incredible 242 not out against West Indies in Sylhet, becoming Bangladesh's highest-ever Test scorer and the first to convert a maiden century into a double ton.
details: Tawhid Hridoy played a historic innings of 242 not out against the West Indies in the second Test in Sylhet, setting a new national record for the highest individual score in Test cricket. He came to the crease when Bangladesh were struggling at 88 for 3 and guided them to a first-innings lead of 30 runs, finishing on 386 for 9.

Hridoy's monumental knock surpassed Mushfiqur Rahim's previous record of 219 not out, achieved against Zimbabwe in 2018. He also became the first Bangladeshi batter to convert his maiden Test century into a double hundred, a remarkable feat in his career.

The young batsman's innings was studded with 11 sixes, just one short of the world record held jointly by Wasim Akram and Yashasvi Jaiswal. He joined an elite club of Bangladeshi Test double-centurions, including Mushfiqur Rahim, Shakib Al Hasan, and Tamim Iqbal.

Hridoy's record-breaking performance also marked several other firsts: it was the first Test double-century by a Bangladeshi against the West Indies, the first at Sylhet International Cricket Stadium, and the first in the World Test Championship for Bangladesh. His maiden century score of 181 also broke Mominul Haque's previous record.

He found crucial support from Taijul Islam, who scored 22, and Taskin Ahmed, who added 12. The pair forged a record eighth-wicket partnership of 117 runs off 167 balls at the Sylhet venue. Shadman Islam was unable to bat due to injury, meaning Bangladesh's innings closed with nine wickets down.

headline_marked: [[Newborn allegedly burned]] in NICU at private Dhaka hospital
headline: Newborn allegedly burned in NICU at private Dhaka hospital
summary: A baby boy's life is in danger after he was reportedly burned due to excessive heat or a short circuit in a private hospital's neonatal intensive care unit.
details: A newborn baby boy was allegedly burned in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) of Royal Care Hospital in Chankharpul, Dhaka, on Saturday.
The baby's father, Golam Rabbani, reported that he heard screams of 'fire' shortly after the child was admitted to the NICU, only to find the baby's head, back, and legs burned.
Rabbani alleges that the incident was caused by excessive heat in the NICU and extreme negligence by the hospital authorities, claiming the damage occurred within two minutes.
The baby was rushed to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery and later admitted to the Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) NICU, where his chances of survival are reportedly slim.
The father further alleged that hospital staff and the owner's brother behaved aggressively toward them when they protested the incident.
Royal Care Hospital owner Aparna Haldar denied negligence, attributing the incident to a electrical short circuit and stating that necessary medical measures are being taken.
The family is seeking legal action and plans to file a case against the hospital authorities.
caption:
A newborn's life hangs in the balance after being allegedly burned in a private hospital's NICU.

Rabbani alleges that the incident was caused by excessive heat in the NICU and extreme negligence by the hospital authorities, claiming the damage occurred within two minutes.

The baby was rushed to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery and later admitted to the Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) NICU, where his chances of survival are reportedly slim.

The father further alleged that hospital staff and the owner's brother behaved aggressively toward them when they protested the incident.

Royal Care Hospital owner Aparna Haldar denied negligence, attributing the incident to a electrical short circuit and stating that necessary medical measures are being taken.

The family is seeking legal action and plans to file a case against the hospital authorities.
